description:
We are a passionate and innovative team of young engineering students driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared ambition to solve real-world challenges through science, technology, and innovation.

Our team brings together fresh perspectives, problem-solving abilities, teamwork, and a strong willingness to learn. We are excited to explore NASA's open-source datasets, develop creative solutions, and transform innovative ideas into meaningful projects.
summary:
Echoes of Space – The Stories Left Behind

Echoes of Space is an interactive, cinematic educational website that explores the human-made hardware, scientific instruments, and mission equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. It transforms NASA mission information into engaging stories, helping visitors discover what spacecraft and exploration missions leave behind after completing their objectives.

The platform features a mission archive, individual mission story pages, an AI-powered storyteller, and interactive quizzes. Through verified NASA data, visitors can explore the history, scientific purpose, and significance of space exploration hardware while learning about the missions that carried it there. The AI storyteller makes complex scientific information easier to understand, while quizzes encourage active learning and knowledge retention.

Echoes of Space addresses the challenge by bringing attention to the often-overlooked legacy of space exploration. It demonstrates that exploration does not end when a mission is over: the hardware, discoveries, and stories it leaves behind continue to contribute to our understanding of the universe.
details:
Project tagline: Every machine leaves a legacy.

1. Project overview

Echoes of Space is an interactive, cinematic digital museum that tells the stories of NASA spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments left on the Moon, Mars and beyond.

The project focuses on the challenge Abandoned but not Forgotten. It helps students and space enthusiasts understand what happened to space exploration hardware after its primary mission, why it was sent into space, what it accomplished and what scientific value it continues to provide.

2. Problem statement

Space exploration has produced thousands of fascinating engineering achievements. However:

  • Many people know about famous missions but not the hardware left behind.
  • NASA mission archives contain technical information that can be difficult for beginners.
  • The scientific contributions of inactive and retired equipment are often overlooked.
  • Students need engaging ways to learn about space exploration.

Our solution: Transform mission information into an interactive storytelling experience.

3. Main features

The Legacy of Voyager: Humanity's Greatest Space Mission

1. Cinematic homepage

A visually immersive introduction with a space-themed hero section, orbital animations and exploration timeline.

The Mars Exploration Family Portrait | The Planetary Society

2. 20-mission hardware archive

A searchable collection of selected missions, including their destinations, histories, hardware and operational statuses.

How NASA Scrambled to Add Science Experiments to Israeli, Indian Moon Probes | Space

3. Moon and Mars storybook

Human-centred stories explaining the machines, their missions and scientific discoveries.

Careers | Crane Aerospace & Electronics

4. Interactive 3D spacecraft hangar

Explore spacecraft and rover models with different viewing angles and lighting.

NASA Prepares for Moon and Mars With New Addition to Its Deep Space Network | NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)

5. Echo AI storyteller

An AI-powered educational assistant that explains mission histories and answers questions using verified NASA information.

Solar System Explorer - learn n play | Devpost

6. Quiz and achievement system

Interactive questions, exploration challenges and badges to encourage learning.

4. Mission collection

The original project brief identifies 20 exhibits:

Destination

Example missions

Moon

Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Eagle, Apollo 15 LRV, LRO

Mars

Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, InSight, Ingenuity, Perseverance

Deep space

Pioneer 10, Voyager 1, Voyager 2, Galileo, Cassini, New Horizons

Other space missions

Kepler, Parker Solar Probe

The collection should distinguish between active, inactive, completed and physically abandoned hardware. These categories are not interchangeable.

6. NASA data sources

Our project can use:

  • NASA Science – Mission and science information
  • NASA Image and Video Library – NASA imagery
  • NASA Planetary Data System – Planetary scientific data
  • International Laser Ranging Service – Lunar laser-ranging information
  • NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory – Mission and engineering information

7. Why is this project important?

  1. Education: Makes space science accessible to beginners.
  2. Preservation: Highlights the legacy of human-made space hardware.
  3. Scientific awareness: Connects hardware to real scientific discoveries.
  4. Inspiration: Encourages young people to explore engineering and astronomy.
  5. Open science: Directs users towards publicly available NASA information.

8. What makes Echoes of Space special?

Our central idea is to turn a technical archive into a digital museum.

Instead of simply showing a spacecraft's name and specifications, we tell its story:

  • Why was it built?
  • What was its mission?
  • What did it discover?
  • What happened to it?
  • Why should we remember it?

The central message:

A mission may end, but its legacy never disappears.
